Subject: Privacy & access: evidence request and next steps

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a clear handoff for your security and legal teams.

Recap (what we covered)
- Finovo asks: PII handling, retention windows by data class, and how support engineers access troubleshooting data.
- Redwood: we described per-customer RBAC, attribute-based filters for logs, tokenized identifiers for analytics, and optional regional-residency pins.

Requests from Finovo that we agreed to deliver
1) Evidence of logging and auth events for support access (sample logs)
2) Documentation of data retention controls by data type and how retention can be configured per tenant
3) Description of escalation / emergency access (what controls, approval chain, and audit trails)

Proposed next steps
- We will provide: SOC2 summary, retention matrix CSV, and a redacted sample of authz/log events for an example tenant. (Deliver by EOD tomorrow.)
- Finovo legal to confirm whether they need full unredacted logs or a redacted sample for initial review.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through the artifacts and answer technical questions.

If that looks right, I’ll send the artifacts to the Drive link and schedule time with your team.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(650) 555-0192

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@finovo.com>

Subject: Re: Privacy & access: evidence request and next steps

Ben — thanks for the summary, this is helpful. A few clarifying points so we deliver the right scope to legal/security: 

1) For the sample logs, we need event-level entries showing: actor id, role, action (read/write/impersonate), resource id, timestamp, and the approval id for any elevated access. Redacted tenant IDs are fine as long as the structure is preserved.
2) Retention matrix: please include default retention and the API/console controls for overriding retention per customer. We also want the default deletion flow (soft delete -> purge) and whether purge is immediate or scheduled.
3) Emergency access: we need the exact approval workflow (who clicks approve), and whether approvals are recorded in an immutable audit log with hashes or just in DB rows.

On scope: for now, redacted samples are fine — legal will ask for specifics if they need unredacted for an audit.

Can you include a short note on where logs are stored (cloud provider + region) and retention of operational logs vs. application logs?

We’re good to meet Wed afternoon; I’ll pull calendar options once I have the artifacts.

— Olivia
Sr. Information Security Lead, Finovo
olivia.park@finovo.com

Hi Olivia —

Adding the artifacts we discussed. Notes inline below each item.

Attachments (links and stubs)
- SOC2-Type2-summary-2026-06.pdf -> high-level controls summary; control IDs map to our internal control catalog. (See attachment.)
- redwood-retention-matrix-2026.csv -> per-data-class default retention, configurable knobs, and API endpoints for tenant overrides. First tab = PII/data-subject mapping; second tab = deletion lifecycle.
- authz-sample-logs-2026.txt -> redacted authz events for a simulated tenant (fields: ts, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_id, approval_id).

Quick answers to your questions:
- Storage/region: logs and customer data are stored in the customer's pinned cloud region by default for Private deployments. For Hosted customers in the US, we store in us-west-2. Operational/logging retention differs: operational traces (metrics/traces) are 30 days default; audit/auth logs are 1 year by default but configurable per contract.
- Emergency access: We support a two-step break-glass flow — engineer requests access via console -> automated ticket created -> manager review (can be auto-approved by SOC rotation for critical incidents) -> access granted for a time-bound window. Every step emits an immutable audit event with a SHA256 hash recorded in our append-only audit store.
- RBAC model: role-first model with optional attribute filters (tenant_id scope enforced at the datastore layer). Support engineers have a scoped role; read-only tickets for debugging use a time-limited proxy token.

Deliverables: I uploaded the three files to the Drive link Ben will share and added the authz sample as a paste in case the drive link has restrictions.

Next actions
- Ben: confirm drive link + send calendar invites for Wed 08/12 (we have availability 09:30–11:30 PT).
- Olivia/Carlos: confirm if legal wants unredacted logs or the redacted sample for initial review.
- Rishi/Marissa: be ready to join the walkthrough and answer any architectural questions.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben / team —

Received the artifacts, thank you. Carlos and I reviewed the redacted logs and the retention matrix; both look aligned with what we need for our first pass. Legal is OK to proceed with the redacted sample for now — they may request limited unredacted records under NDA if we proceed to procurement.

Please schedule a 30-min walkthrough on Wed 08/12 at 10:30 AM PT (that works for our side). Key items we’ll validate in the call:
- Walk through a single authz event end-to-end (who requested, how it was approved, and how the event is immutable in the audit store)
- Show API calls / console flow for adjusting retention per-tenant
- Confirm how support engineers are scoped and how time-limited proxy tokens are issued for debugging

If you can add a short diagram (1 slide) showing the emergency access approval chain, that will expedite legal’s final questions.

See you at 10:30.

— Olivia
Sr. Information Security Lead, Finovo
